content: WorldSync experiment finding from reproduction/INTEGRATION.md, section 'Audit notes that must travel with the code'. KV retention (worldsync/lingbotkvretention.py): an independent audit confirmed three real defects. Selection is made once per. layer on the first, highest-noise attention call, so the query is content-blind in early layers; the gate hard-codes the. 18/6 window, so other windows silently run stock attention; and the archive is unbounded full-precision per-layer KV on CPU,. about 1.3 GB per latent frame (roughly 200 GB over 40 chunks). The bounded --budget-memory method fixes these. DeCoPrune port: deviates from the released runtime (no observed-prefix probe; real RoPE kept for q0 <= 17; attention rebuilt per layer from our own archive; threshold not re-tuned). Two seeds only. Seed noise on stock under the. alternative schedule moved 0.64 to 0.45. Memory LoRA: trained on 48 pairs for 200 steps; held-out loss fell about the same with and without the memory slot, so it. mostly adapted to the domain.

content: WorldSync experiment finding from reproduction/score-drivers.md, section 'Recommendation: control and dynamics realization'. The single highest-leverage change is making the trajectory actually happen and letting the. player see that it did, ahead of more memory work: The player's state is the commanded pose ("intended camera commands only; not measured visual. motion"), so the player's Keep / Extend / Correct decisions cannot react to a world that moved less. than commanded. Feed it measured motion from visual odometry on the generated frames (realized yaw,. approach scale), and let it Extend or Correct until the realized trajectory meets the plan (yaw within. about 10 degrees, a visible approach). Recalibrate the turn rate to about 68 deg/s so a commanded 180 degrees is realized (realized/commanded. is 0.89-0.92 today). Re-test the S backward action: the judge wants a backward walk in place and gets a camera retreat or a. viewpoint jump (GC024). Why this first: cause 1 covers 56% of scored episodes and every forced-1.0 episode, GC is the only. dimension where the gate swings scores by 2.6 points, and memory (46/6) leaves the verdict counts unchanged. Memory is the second lever, for cause 3 (GC identity drift on revisit), and it only pays once the camera. actually returns. Caveats: 54 scored episodes, one judge, two seeds with up to about 2 points of seed-to-seed variance. (GC015, GC005), a judge that gates strictly (partial vs pass is a judgment call), and no check that. more Extend steps raise translation approach beyond the measured x1.04.

content: WorldSync experiment finding from reproduction/corrected-controller-validation.md, section 'Caveats'. Twelve cases and one seed: a single episode varies by about ±1 point between seeds, so only large differences are informative. The arms differ in more than the controller: text (caption+objective vs objective only; insight caption vs "wait and observe") and chunk budget (40 vs 60 for moving cases). This compares the two complete configurations as specified. Hold-service token cap raised (above). Proxy transport for the player. Episode length differs sharply: the legacy player sends END once the reference plan's legs are done, so its moving-case videos are 5-10 s long; every corrected-arm video runs the full 60 s budget. Short videos leave no time for a revisit, which bears on the out-of-sight gate; long ones give the judge more to fault. Sanity check: the legacy arm's scores equal the frozen Modal stock run's on 7 of 9 moving cases (GC024 4.60 vs 1.00 and GC022 1.80 vs 2.40 differ), so the local legacy arm broadly reproduces the frozen configuration.
label: Experiment finding: Caveats
